stories.title: On-Pi service-control CLI -- stop/start/restart/kill/status each OBD service or ALL (maintenance tool)
acceptance: a CLI utility on the Pi (e.g. scripts/obdctl.sh + a `make`/deploy-installed entrypoint) run as `obdctl <action> <service|all>`; actions: status, start, stop, restart, kill (SIGKILL for a stuck unit). Bare/no-arg invocation = status of ALL (never a destructive default). --help + --dry-run.

CANONICAL UNIT LIST (SSOT, grounded -- the 8 deploy-installed OBD-project units, verified on the Pi 2026-07-27): eclipse-obd, eclipse-powerwatch, eclipse-states-http, eclipse-boot-state, eclipse-dashboard, rfcomm-bind, splash-boot, splash-grace. Derive/share the list from a single source (extend the US-403 service_control.py SERVICE_ALLOWLIST or a shared manifest) so it does NOT drift from what deploy installs -- do NOT hardcode a second divergent list.
short aliases accepted (e.g. `obd`, `powerwatch`, `dashboard`, `states`, `splash`) + the full unit name; `all` targets every unit in the canonical list

SAFETY -- eclipse-powerwatch is the safe-shutdown guard (D-7/F-7 cardinal rule: never leave it stopped or shutdown protection is disabled). stop/kill of powerwatch (directly or via `all`) prints a LOUD warning + requires an explicit confirm (or a --force/--yes flag); restart/status of powerwatch is unrestricted. The tool must make it easy to see powerwatch is down + to bring it back.

SAFETY -- `kill` (SIGKILL) is forceful: require explicit intent (confirm or explicit action word), never a fallback of `stop`; document that kill can leave a unit's resources uncleaned (use stop first, kill only when stuck)

`all` acts in a SENSIBLE ORDER: stop/kill in reverse-dependency order (kiosk/emitters/splash first, then states-http, then the core eclipse-obd/powerwatch last); start in dependency order (states-http before dashboard, etc.) -- avoid races + orphaned kiosks

HONEST OUTPUT: for each targeted unit print before-state -> action -> after-state (active/inactive/failed/not-installed) + a clear per-unit OK/FAIL; `all` prints a summary table; a not-installed unit is reported honestly, not an error-crash; non-zero exit if any requested action failed
privilege handled cleanly (systemctl needs root -- sudo or the existing 51-eclipse-service-control polkit path); the tool tells the operator if it lacks privilege rather than failing cryptically
deploy-installed (deploy-pi.sh) so it's on the Pi after a deploy, on PATH or a known location; documented in deploy/README + a one-line usage in --help
bash -n / shellcheck clean (or ruff if Python); a test exercises the action-dispatch + the canonical-list-vs-deploy-installed consistency + the powerwatch-stop-guard

validationCriteria.action: on the Pi: obdctl status all
validationCriteria.outcome: lists all 8 OBD units with their live state; no crash on any not-installed unit
eclipse-obd restarts; before->after state shown; exit 0
stops the units in reverse-dependency order; powerwatch stop triggers the loud warning + confirm; summary table shows per-unit result
requires explicit intent, SIGKILLs the kiosk, reports killed + after-state inactive
refuses/warns + requires confirm (safe-shutdown-guard protection); restart powerwatch is unrestricted

conditionalOutcomes: if enumerating the canonical unit list from the deploy scripts vs service_control.py reveals a drift (a unit deploy installs that neither list knows), reconcile to ONE SSOT + flag it -- do not silently maintain two lists

eclipse-sync.service appears in the US-403 allow-list but was NOT in the Pi's installed units (2026-07-27) -- confirm whether it's a real unit or folded into eclipse-obd; include only actually-installed units in `all`, report a listed-but-absent unit honestly
stories.goal: As the CIO doing maintenance or debugging on the Pi, I want ONE command I can run on the Pi to stop, start, restart, kill, or status any single OBD-project service OR ALL of them, so I can service the system or work through issues without hand-typing systemctl for each unit + remembering the full unit list.

bigDefinitionOfDone: (on the Pi: obdctl status all) → (lists all 8 OBD units with their live state; no crash on any not-installed unit)  [from US-492]
(obdctl restart obd  (alias)) → (eclipse-obd restarts; before->after state shown; exit 0)  [from US-492]
(obdctl stop all) → (stops the units in reverse-dependency order; powerwatch stop triggers the loud warning + confirm; summary table shows per-unit result)  [from US-492]
(obdctl kill dashboard) → (requires explicit intent, SIGKILLs the kiosk, reports killed + after-state inactive)  [from US-492]
(obdctl stop powerwatch  (without --force)) → (refuses/warns + requires confirm (safe-shutdown-guard protection); restart powerwatch is unrestricted)  [from US-492]
